neighbours.label: ' around' / ' about' / ' along' as a spatial or approximate preposition after a verb or noun (walk around the perimeter, flip it around, expansion along the row, 約/约 approx.)
fire: If the mouse begins to walk clockwise around the perimeter of the table, what happens to the wheel?
Take the formula for the volume of a cube and flip it around to solve for the side length.
The wheel is divided around its perimeter into thirty-eight numbered slots of equal size.
Cofactor expansion along the first row gives the determinant in three short steps.
The farm sends about fifty thousand tons of beets to the eight factories every autumn.
The tourists wandered around the old harbor and then walked along the river until sunset.
The rope was wrapped around the post twice and then pulled tight along the edge of the dock.
Turn the picture around and look at it again from the other side of the table.
quiet: Suppose the mouse begins to walk toward the cheese, what happens to the wheel on the table?
Use the formula for the volume of a cube and solve it for the side length of the box.
Thirty-eight numbered slots of equal size and two colors make up the wheel.
Expanding the first row by cofactors gives the determinant in three short steps.
Every autumn the farm sends fifty thousand tons of beets to the eight factories.
Tourists visited the old harbor and then reached the river just before sunset.
Twice the rope was tied to the post and then pulled tight at the edge of the dock.
Look at the picture again from the other side of the table and tell me what you see.
